description: These are the best ribs I think I have ever made. They are fall off the bone tender and juicy with a tangy/spicy sauce that we loved. I started with a recipe from my Weber's Big Book of Grilling, tweaked it to our liking and experimented on the grill and finally, after 4-5 tries, came up with the perfect Baby Back Rib recipe, IMHO. Thus the name, Nimrod's Baby Back Ribs. For a hickory flavor, soak 2 handfulls of Hickory Chips in water for at least 30 minutes and add to the hot coals the last 30 minutes of grilling. I was hoping to get the cooking time exact, but it varied each time I made these. Hope you enjoy. Be sure to have lots of napkins on hand cause you will need them. You also will need a grill that you can cook using indirect heat.
ingredients: ["1 tablespoon olive oil", "1/4 cup finely chopped yellow onion", "2 teaspoons minced garlic (by all means use more if you like)", "3/4 cup ketchup", "1/2 cup rice vinegar (please use rice vinegar with no substitutions because it makes a difference IMO)", "1/4 cup firmly packed light brown sugar", "3 tablespoons Worcestershire sauce", "1 1/2 tablespoons yellow mustard", "3 teaspoons soy sauce", "1/2 teaspoon chili powder", "Tabasco sauce", "4 lbs pork baby back ribs (2-3 racks)", "kosher salt", "fresh ground black pepper"]
steps: ["To make the Sauce: In a medium saucepan over medium-high, warm the vegetable oil. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, until translucent, 4-5 minutes.", "Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.", "Add the remaining sauce ingredients, including Tabasco sauce to taste, and bring to a boil.", "Reduce heat and simmer for about 15 minutes. description: Traditionally Greek. Always good. Once baked, the baklava has to stand for 3 hours to overnight to absorb the syrup into its layers. Whereas it is most common to find baklava made entirely with walnuts here in Greece, I prefer a combination with almonds. Sometimes I'll make the baklava using pistachios, or sometimes a 1/2-1/2 mixture of pistachios and almonds. They're all great variations on a delicious theme.
ingredients: ["2 cups honey (preferably Greek thyme honey, but no biggy if you can\\u0027t get it. Remove peels and cinnamon sticks and allow to come to room temperature before using.", "Combine walnuts, almonds, sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ground cloves and 3 tablespoons melted butter together in a bowl and mix thoroughly.", "Place phyllo between sheets of waxed paper and cover with a slightly damp towel to prevent phyllo from drying out. Brush bottom and sides of an 18x12-inch inch pan generously with melted butter.", "Place 8 phyllo sheets into bottom of pan, brushing each sheet generously with butter. Fold over the overlapping phyllo sheets brushing each with butter, to envelop the nut mixture.", "Repeat layering process 2 more times to form 3 nut layers.", "Top pastry with remaining phyllo dough and generously brush top layer with melted butter. Stud each diamond-shaped piece (and any odd looking ones near the ends of the pan) in the centre with a whole clove per piece. Pour remaining melted butter over pastry and lightly sprinkle some water on top too (wet your hand under the tap twice and shake this out over the pastry).", "Bake pastry in a 325°F oven for 1 hour to 75 minutes, until nicely golden-brown. description: Carpaccio of beef was created by Giuseppe Cipriani of Harry's Bar in Venice, and has become famous throughout the world as being typical of modern Italian cuisine. There are an unlimited number of variations of this dish, but often the simpler the better. This variation tops the tender beef slices with crisp, vibrant watercress and a drizzle of garlicky aioli sauce to finish. Serve as a light lunch dish, or as an appetizer.

description: This is steak tartare as we use to make it in Sweden. It is mixed at the table by the guests themselves. It is best served with ice-cold vodka or Champagne (but then cut down on the accessories). The quality of the meat cannot be compromised upon. Use only fresh fillet. One popular variety is to let the guests mix their steaks and then broil them on very high heat over a charcoal fire for only a few seconds, so that they remain raw inside. In that case it may be served with french fries and butter Maitre d'Hotel (i.e. butter mixed with finely chopped parsley and a little lemon).

recipe_title: Freshly Shucked Oysters and Sauce Mignonette With a Twist!
description: A classic with a twist - I like to add a splash or three of Tabasco sauce to my shallot and red wine vinegar Mignonette sauce, for that extra zap! Cut the muscle attachment to lower shell. description: Seaweed has amazing properties! Sea vegetables are virtually fat-free, low calorie and are one of the richest sources of minerals in the vegetable kingdom. According to Seibin and Teruko Arasaki, authors of Vegetables from the Sea, “All of the minerals required by human beings, including calcium, sodium, magnesium, potassium, iodine, iron, and zinc are present in sufficient amounts. In addition, there are many trace elements in seaweeds.” They also contain vitamins as vitamin A (in the form of beta-carotene), B1, B2, B6, niacin, vitamin C, pantothenic acid, and folic acid. Analysis has shown trace amounts of vitamin B12, which rarely occurs in land vegetables. Sea vegetables have been shown to cleanse the body of toxic pollutants. Seaweed feeds the shafts and the ducts of the scalp to help improve the health of the hair. It has been said that the thick, black, lustrous hair of the Japanese is partly due to their regular diet of brown sea vegetables such as arame. Research has shown that minerals are important to healthy hair growth, and arame has a high mineral content. Other health benefits, according to Carlson Wade’s book Health Secrets from the Orient, include regulating the hormones, enriching the bloodstream, assisting in metabolism, promoting a youthful skin color, and helping to warm the body to promote mental youthfulness. So enjoy this nutritionally-packed food on the planet.
ingredients: ["3/4 ounce dried wakame seaweed (whole or cut)", "3 tablespoons rice vinegar (not seasoned)", "3 tablespoons soy sauce", "1 tablespoon sesame oil", "1 teaspoon sugar", "red pepper flakes", "1 teaspoon finely grated ginger", "1/2 teaspoon minced garlic", "2 scallions, thinly sliced", "1/4 cup shredded carrot", "2 tablespoons chopped fresh cilantro", "1 tablespoon sesame seeds, toasted"]

dish_name: Borbor tnaot (sweet palm fruit tapioca pudding)
recipe_title: Borbor tnaot, warm sweet sugar palm fruit pudding with coconut cream (បបរត្នោត)
description: Traditional Cambodian dessert featuring tender translucent palm fruit seeds simmered with tapioca pearls, palm sugar, and coconut milk.
ingredients: ["300 g fresh sugar palm fruit (plae tnaot), peeled and sliced", "½ cup small tapioca pearls", "600 ml water", "120 g Cambodian palm sugar", "250 ml thick coconut milk", "½ tsp salt", "2 pandan leaves, tied in a knot"]
steps: ["Soak tapioca pearls in water for 15 minutes.", "Bring water to a boil in a saucepan with pandan leaves and palm sugar until melted.", "Add soaked tapioca pearls and simmer on medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until tapioca turns translucent.", "Add sliced sugar palm fruit and simmer for 5 minutes.", "In a separate small pot, warm coconut milk with salt.", "Ladle sweet warm palm fruit tapioca into bowls, spoon salted coconut cream over top, and serve warm."]
dish_name_kh: បបរត្នោត

dish_name: Cha kdam kroeung (stir-fried crab in red kroeung)
recipe_title: Cha kdam kroeung, fresh crabs wok-tossed in aromatic red kroeung (ក្តាមឆាគ្រឿង)
description: Fragrant, spicy stir-fried sea crabs in rich lemongrass-turmeric paste, finished with coconut milk and holy basil.
ingredients: ["2 whole blue crabs, cleaned and quartered (claws cracked)", "Kroeung: 2 stalks lemongrass, thinly sliced, 3 cm galangal, sliced, 3 cm fresh turmeric (or 1 tsp ground), 4 kaffir lime leaves, stems removed, 4 cloves garlic, 3 shallots, 5 dried red chillies, soaked", "100 ml coconut milk", "1 tbsp fish sauce", "1 tbsp palm sugar", "1 onion, cut into wedges", "1 handful holy basil leaves", "2 tbsp vegetable oil"]
steps: ["Pound the red kroeung into a fine paste.", "Heat oil in a wok over medium-high heat and fry red kroeung for 2 minutes until fragrant.", "Add crab pieces and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes until shells turn bright orange.", "Pour in coconut milk, fish sauce, palm sugar and onion wedges; toss, cover and steam for 3 minutes until crab is cooked through.", "Fold in holy basil leaves, toss until wilted and fragrant, and serve hot with jasmine rice."]
dish_name_kh: ក្តាមឆាគ្រឿង

dish_name: Sngor trey bampe (clear fish soup with tamarind leaves)
recipe_title: Sngor trey sleuk ampil, clear river fish soup with young tamarind leaves (ស្ងោរជ្រក់ត្រីស្លឹកអម្ពិល)
description: Delicate sour soup made with sweet freshwater fish, fragrant young tamarind leaves, lemongrass, and fresh herbs.
ingredients: ["500 g freshwater fish steaks (catfish or snakehead), cleaned", "1.2 litres water", "1 cup young tender tamarind leaves (sleuk ampil kchey)", "2 stalks lemongrass, bruised", "3 shallots, crushed", "4 cloves garlic", "1 thumb galangal, sliced", "2 tbsp fish sauce", "1 tsp sugar", "½ tsp salt", "Rice paddy herb (ma-om) and bird's eye chillies, to serve"]
steps: ["Bring water to a boil in a pot with lemongrass, galangal, crushed shallots and garlic for 5 minutes.", "Add fish steaks and simmer gently on medium heat for 8–10 minutes until tender, skimming off foam.", "Add young tamarind leaves and simmer for 2 minutes to impart their natural citrusy tang.", "Season with fish sauce, sugar and salt to create a refreshing sour balance.", "Turn off heat, add chopped ma-om and crushed chillies, and serve steaming hot with rice."]
dish_name_kh: ស្ងោរជ្រក់ត្រីស្លឹកអម្ពិល
